metadata.title: Use of a Drug Master File for Shared System REMS Submissions Guidance for Industry
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: The use of a DMF is not a requirement for SSRs. However, if applicants that are subject to and 22 participating in an SSR choose to use a DMF, this guidance provides an overview of a 23 recommended approach for their SSR submissions. Additional and more-detailed submission 24 instructions are included in a separate technical guide, Technical Conformance Guide for Shared 25 System REMS Drug Master File Submissions (the SSR DMF Technical Conformance Guide) , 26 which will be updated periodically. 5
candidates.context: This guidance provides recommendations for applicants that are part of a shared system risk 18 evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) on using an electronic Type V 2 Drug Master File 19 (DMF) 3 for shared system REMS (SSR) submissions. The recommendations in this guidance are 20 intended to improve the efficiency of submitting SSR to the Agency. 4 1 This guidance has been prepared by the Office of Medication Error Prevention and Risk Management, Office of Surveillance and Epidemiology, in collaboration with other Offices in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research and with the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER), at the Food and Drug Administration.

candidates.statement: A REMS is a required risk management plan that uses tools beyond the FDA-approved 42 prescribing information to ensure that the benefits of certain drugs 7 outweigh their risks. 8 FDA 43 can, under certain circumstances, 9 require that the REMS for a drug include one or more 44 elements to assure safe use (ETASU). 10 When ETASUs are required for an innovator drug, any 45 abbreviated new drug application (ANDA) 11 referencing that innovator drug must use an SSR 46 with the innovator (unless FDA waives the requirement for using a shared system). 12 There are 47 also circumstances under which multiple applicants form an SSR to minimize the burden on the 48 health care delivery system, such as for a class of similar products. 49 ________________________

candidates.statement: As part of an SSR, multiple applicants need to coordinate the submission of identical REMS- 56 related documents by each applicant to its own application. To improve the efficiency of the 57 submission and review process for SSRs, FDA recommends that applicants use a Type V DMF 58 for their SSR submissions. As noted above, as of the date specified by FDA, applicants who 59 choose to use a Type V DMF for an SSR must make the DMF submissions electronically, as 60 required in the binding guidance for industry on Providing Regulatory Submissions in Electronic 61 Format — Certain Human Pharmaceutical Product Applications and Related Submissions Using 62 the eCTD Specifications (Revision 4). 63 In addition to the recommendations provided in this guidance, FDA advises stakeholders to refer 64 to other relevant FDA resources to help create their submissions, such as the following: 65
candidates.context: A DMF is a voluntary submission that may be used to provide confidential detailed information 50 to the Agency. 13 The DMF holder may authorize other applicants to reference information in the 51 holder’s DMF. A DMF is submitted solely at the discretion of the DMF holder, and the 52 technical contents of a DMF are customarily reviewed by FDA only in connection with the 53 review of an application. There are several types of DMFs; a Type V is used for “FDA-accepted 54 reference information.” 14 • Technical Conformance Guide for Shared System REMS Drug Master File Submissions 15

candidates.statement: A. Ownership of the SSR DMF 85 The owner of the SSR DMF is the DMF holder who is jointly designated by the SSR applicants. 86 Only one company should be listed as the DMF holder. The DMF holder will make submissions 87 to the DMF on behalf of the SSR applicants. Therefore, FDA will consider any submission to 88 the SSR DMF to represent the views of the participating SSR applicants. 89

candidates.statement: C. Authorization To Refer to the SSR DMF 100 The DMF holder must submit letters of authorization (LOAs) to the DMF that permit FDA to 101 review information in the DMF in support of the SSR applicants’ applications. 24 The DMF 102 holder should submit a separate LOA to the DMF for each SSR applicant. If an SSR applicant is 103 also the DMF holder, an LOA should still be submitted to the DMF. The DMF holder does not 104 need to submit a new LOA for each new submission to the DMF unless there is a change in the 105 DMF holder name or the authorized party name. 106 The DMF holder should also send a copy of the LOA to each SSR applicant who has been 107 authorized to incorporate the information contained in the DMF by reference. Each SSR 108 applicant should then submit the copy of the LOA to its own application. 25 SSR applicants only 109 need to submit this LOA to their application one time unless there is a change in the DMF holder 110 name or the authorized party name. 111

candidates.statement: The cross-reference submission for a REMS Original, 33 minor REMS modification, 155 major REMS modification, and REMS modification due to safety label changes should 156 be submitted to the individual application as an amendment, if applicable, or a 157 supplement. Submissions of REMS revisions 34 and REMS assessments are not 158 supplemental applications. Therefore, the cross-reference submissions should also not be 159 submitted as supplements. 160
candidates.context: This section provides a brief overview of cross-reference submissions. 146 • A cross-reference submission will be needed after any of the following has been 147 submitted to the SSR DMF: 148 o REMS Original 149 o Minor REMS Modification 150 o Major REMS Modification 151 o REMS Modification Due to Safety Label Changes 152 o REMS Revision 153 o REMS Assessment 32 31 The cross-reference submission serves to “incorporate the material in the DMF by reference.” See section VI.B of the Guideline for Drug Master Files , available at https://www.fda.gov/Drugs/DevelopmentApprovalProcess/FormsSubmissionRequirements/DrugMasterFilesDMFs/ ucm073164.htm .

candidates.statement: • An SSR applicant should submit a copy of the DMF holder’s LOA to its application 171 either before or at the time of the applicant’s first cross-reference submission. As 172 previously described in section III.C Authorization To Refer to the SSR DMF , the SSR 173 applicant should submit this LOA only once, unless there is a change in the DMF holder 174 name or the authorized party name. 175 • To facilitate tracking of the cross-reference submissions, FDA recommends that SSR 176 applicants submit their cross-reference submissions as soon as possible after the DMF 177 holder has made the corresponding submission to the SSR DMF. In addition, FDA 178 recommends that SSR applicants work together to make their cross-reference 179 submissions on the same day. 180

candidates.context: For questions about providing electronic submissions according to the recommendations in this 185 35 Medication Guides that are part of a REMS should be included in each applicant’s cross-reference submission to its NDA/BLA/ANDA. Please note that if changes have been made to the Medication Guide that is part of a REMS, a REMS supplement should be submitted to the application, as well as a cross reference to the DMF. If a product has a Medication Guide that is not part of the REMS, it does not need to be included in any REMS submission.
